requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The field filter in contractless mode is inverted: `field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst` picks readonly fields and skips writable ones. Public mutable fields of T are never serialized, which breaks the requirement's contractless behaviour over public members. Public readonly fields are selected and marked IsWritable: true, so the generated Deserialize assigns to them and Project B fails to compile (CS0191).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementGapTests.PublicWritableField_IsSerialized_AndReadOnlyFieldIsNot. On head it should fail: the generated source has no 'Quantity', and the output compilation reports an error for assigning 'Frozen'.

findings.claim: Acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not implemented. Collect always builds members either contractless (no surrogate) or from the surrogate, and never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember] on T. A referenced type with [IgnoreMember] members still has them serialized under name keys. Its int-keyed contract is replaced by string keys, so the wire format differs from what the dynamic/standard resolver produces for the same type.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterRequirementGapTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. On head the generated formatter references 'SecretValue', which is marked [IgnoreMember] on the referenced type.

findings.claim: The field filter in `IsPublicReadWrite` is inverted: it reads `field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst` instead of `!field.IsReadOnly`. In contractless mode an ordinary mutable field such as `public int MutableField;` is silently dropped from the wire format. A `public readonly int ReadOnlyField;` is selected instead and gets `IsWritable: true`. The generated Deserialize then assigns the readonly field, so the consuming project fails to compile (CS0191). The same filter makes surrogate mode reject mutable fields with MsgPack022 and accept readonly ones.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterFieldTests.ContractlessMode_SerializesMutableFields_AndCompiles. ProjectA declares a type with a mutable and a readonly public field. ProjectB declares `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` for it. The test asserts the generated source mentions MutableField and the output compilation has no errors. Expected to fail on head.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats a public field as eligible only when field.IsReadOnly is true, which is inverted. Writable public fields are skipped and readonly fields are included, so the generated deserializer would assign to readonly fields (compile error CS0191 in the user's project). Contractless mode would also miss normal public fields, contradicting the documented behavior.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator snapshot test for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> where T has `public int A;` and `public readonly int B;`. Check that A is emitted and B is not, then compile the output.

hunches.claim: Constructor parameters are always passed as empty and members are all marked writable. The generated code therefore requires a parameterless constructor, and for structs it relies on init/required handling. Types with only a parameterized constructor or get-only properties get no formatter, and a required or init-only property may produce uncompilable output. The documented 'public read-write' limit makes this partly intended.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a type with `public required string P {get;set;}` and for one with `init`-only properties. Compile the output and compare it with the diagnostics.

hunches.claim: New diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added to the analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics, but the generator reports them in the generator itself (RegisterSourceOutput) rather than the analyzer. The AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md and the docs under doc/analyzers/ for the new ids are not part of the diff, so the release tracking analyzer (RS2000) and the help links (404) may break the build. The reported diagnostics also reuse existing ids such as NoDeserializingConstructor, MemberNeedsKey and KeysMustBeUnique, with a mismatched message format argument count (NoDeserializingConstructor is created with no args).

receipt_plan.detail: Build the SourceGenerator project, which has the Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers release tracking enabled, and check for RS2000/RS2002 warnings. Add a test that triggers NoDeserializingConstructor on a formatter and confirm the message formats without error.

hunches.claim: In contractless mode, the key order is alphabetical (OrderBy name) and string keys are used with no attributes honored on T. The requirement says that attributes on T are honored if present, but the collector never reads [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] or [DataMember] on T.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a type annotated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] on its members, or with [IgnoreMember] on a public property. Serialize and check that the keys and membership follow the attributes.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats public fields as eligible only when field.IsReadOnly is true (inverted). Writable public fields are skipped, and readonly fields are marked IsWritable: true. The generated deserializer then assigns to readonly fields, so the generated formatter will fail to compile (CS0191) or the contractless contract will silently drop data. The inversion is not a security issue by itself, but it is a correctness defect in deserialization of untrusted data shape.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator snapshot test: [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class for a type with `public int Field;` and `public readonly int RO;`. Expect Field serialized and RO excluded; the test fails: Field is dropped and RO produces a compile error.

hunches.claim: In contractless mode, string-key members are sorted by name and given an IntKey of their index, but isIntKey=false. That is fine, but surrogate int keys with gaps (e.g. 0 and 1000) pass an attacker-irrelevant but unbounded IntKey into the array-layout templates. The array-header size is derived from the max key, so a very large [Key(int.MaxValue)] on a surrogate would make generated code allocate or write a huge array header. Deserialization of an array of that declared length then loops over attacker-supplied header counts; the existing MessagePackSecurity and collection checks do not apply to the generated object formatter's header count.

receipt_plan.detail: Snapshot test: surrogate with [Key(0)] and [Key(100000)]. Inspect the generated Serialize writing an array header of 100001 nil elements, and compare with the existing [MessagePackObject] behaviour.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats a public field as writable only when field.IsReadOnly is true, which is inverted. Public mutable fields are skipped and readonly fields are included. This contradicts the documented contractless behaviour of serializing public read-write properties and fields. Readonly fields will fail at deserialization, or the generated code will not compile.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type with `public int F;` and a formatter for it. Assert that F round-trips; the test currently fails. Also add a type with `public readonly int R;` and check that the generated code compiles.

hunches.claim: IsPublicReadWrite treats a public field as writable only if it is readonly (`field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`). That is almost certainly inverted. Ordinary mutable public fields are skipped, and readonly fields are included and then assigned in generated code, which would not compile. No test has a public field on a formatted type, so nothing would notice.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:271 negate-condition: field.IsReadOnly -> !field.IsReadOnly; expected to survive because every External* test type uses only auto-properties and no test has a public field. Add a type with `public int F;` to prove it.

hunches.claim: The contractless tests never check that the generated output actually uses the intended ordering and keys. Members are sorted with OrderBy(Name, Ordinal), but the tests only check a round trip, the 0x82 map header and JSON contents. Removing the OrderBy, or swapping intKey and stringKey, would not fail any test.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:131 delete-statement: remove .OrderBy(m => m.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal); expected to survive because tests assert neither order nor exact bytes and JSON checks use Contains.

hunches.claim: Generated-output diagnostics are tested only in part. There are no snapshot or regeneration tests of the emitted partial class. In particular, the template change `partial class` vs `internal sealed class` is covered only indirectly through ExecutionTests. Nothing checks that nested or namespaced user formatters, or the `IsUserDeclaredFormatter` branch in either template, produce valid output. The Equals change for IsUserDeclaredFormatter also has no test.

receipt_plan.detail: ObjectSerializationInfo.cs:168 delete-statement: remove `&& IsUserDeclaredFormatter == other.IsUserDeclaredFormatter`; expected to survive because no test compares two infos differing only in this flag.

hunches.claim: The diagnostic tests do not cover important rejection branches. Missing: a class data type with no accessible parameterless constructor (NoDeserializingConstructor), duplicate surrogate keys (KeysMustBeUnique), a surrogate member lacking [Key] (MemberNeedsKey), an inaccessible type, a generic type, and a formatter implementing multiple IMessagePackFormatter<T> interfaces. Deleting any of these guards would pass the tests.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:75 remove-guard: delete the `isClass && !InstanceConstructors.Any(...)` block; expected to survive because no test uses a type without a parameterless constructor.

hunches.claim: The GeneratedFormatterAttribute filter in GeneratorUtilities, which excludes attributed formatters from hand-written registration, is covered only by GeneratedFormattersAreRegisteredInGeneratedResolver. That test would also pass if the same formatter were registered twice. No test would catch duplicate registration or the guard being removed.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` clause; expected to survive or fail only through duplicate-registration compile errors, which no dedicated test checks.

hunches.claim: Surrogate mode with string keys is untested in execution tests (the only surrogate uses int keys). The branch `CreateMember(target, intKey: members.Count, stringKey: (string)key)` and the `isIntKey=false` path are unexercised. Also the int-key gap behavior (keys 3 and 7) is checked only by array length 8, not by slot placement.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:176 swap-boolean: stringKey: (string)key -> target.Name; expected to survive because no test uses a string-key surrogate.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` only checks the formatter class itself. When the formatter is nested in a non-partial containing type (e.g. `class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`), the templates emit the nesting via `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces`. If that emits `partial class Outer`, the user gets a CS0260-style compile error instead of MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:292-299) inspects only formatter.DeclaringSyntaxReferences and never ContainingType. The templates (FormatterTemplate.tt:11, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:17) wrap the declaration in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces.

hunches.claim: The `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` predicate accepts only `ClassDeclarationSyntax`, but the attribute is `AttributeTargets.Class`, which also permits record classes. `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` is silently skipped: no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic, only CS0535 errors for the unimplemented interface members.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:31 uses `predicate: static (node, _) => node is ClassDeclarationSyntax`. RecordDeclarationSyntax does not derive from ClassDeclarationSyntax, so a record formatter never reaches GeneratedFormatterCollector and no diagnostic is reported.

hunches.claim: The generated formatter is emitted as `partial class` with no accessibility modifier. In the existing template the generated formatter is also registered in the source-generated resolver. A user's `public partial class` merges fine, but if the user class is nested or has `sealed`/`static`/other modifiers that differ from the emitted ones, nothing is emitted that preserves them. The generated file also drops type constraints for the formatter class, which is harmless. Because the class is also listed in the resolver, the resolver may now start returning the formatter for T in existing projects. Without opting in, an existing project that happens to add the attribute changes formatter selection for T, which is the intended opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that the resolver template emits registration of Info.Formatter for IsUserDeclaredFormatter infos, and that the class name is not duplicated with the user's declared type in a nested-type case.

hunches.claim: The generated formatter model is built by the generator with reportDiagnostic: null, and failures return null silently. A separate diagnostics pipeline re-runs Collect. If ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate fails, no diagnostic is reported, and the formatter is silently not generated. The user-declared partial class then fails to implement IMessagePackFormatter<T> with only a generic compiler error. This is not a security protection being disabled, only a degraded diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the generatedFormatterDiagnostics SelectMany: when ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate returns false, it emits an empty array.

hunches.claim: The new MsgPack019-022 diagnostics are only reported by the source generator via ReportDiagnostic. They are not added to the analyzer, and the pre-existing MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer was not changed to report them. The diagnostic IDs and descriptors are declared there, so descriptor and report locations are inconsistent.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the SupportedDiagnostics list in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer with where the generator reports the diagnostics. Check whether the analyzer ever reports MsgPack019-022.

hunches.claim: The SurrogateKeysMustNotMixStringAndInt test expects MsgPack005 at the Name member. The code under test reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys in the new collector, and that diagnostic fires only if the descriptor id is MsgPack005. The test also leaves the surrogate's own compile state with no other expected diagnostics. Meanwhile, no test covers the opposite case, where all keys are the same kind and nothing is reported.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys == MsgPack005 and add a positive test with consistent surrogate keys.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The change generates a formatter for a type from a referenced assembly, which looks like it contradicts the TypeCollector rule that metadata-only types get no formatter from the compiling assembly. Ledger L11 says that rule is deliberate and covers only automatic collection. The new path is explicit opt-in through a partial formatter class and never goes through CollectCore, so the two do not conflict.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] metadata-only types are deliberately skipped by TypeCollector.CollectCore. GeneratedFormatterCollector is a separate explicit opt-in path, so there is no contradiction.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=docs: Requiring the MessagePackObject annotation by default is intentional, to enforce explicitness. (source: README.md) (would-be finding: Contractless mode is the default for types without attributes, with no [MessagePackObject] required. This looks like it breaks the explicitness convention in L8, but the opt-in [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute is itself the explicit marker, so the convention holds.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] requiring MessagePackObject is intentional to enforce explicitness. The explicit [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] attribute provides that explicitness.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] with an optional SurrogateType property, where a user-defined surrogate type in Project B mirrors T's shape and keys are mapped by property name, so attribute-based keys and Union settings can be supplied without touching Project A. Code: Attribute has a SurrogateType property; generator reads keys/union attributes from the surrogate and emits conversion code between T and the surrogate, which the contractless-only reading would not do.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>, generating a contractless formatter over T's public members (honouring any MessagePack attributes present) in the declaring assembly, with no surrogate type. Code: Generator discovers classes with the attribute, reads T from the IMessagePackFormatter<T> interface, and emits Serialize/Deserialize directly for T's public members, defaulting to contractless when T has no [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract]; no SurrogateType property.
